A.claim: Classical Fermat descent on the all-even branch sends signature (2r,2s,2t) to signature (2r,2r,t) with coefficient 2 - it diagonalises the left exponents, halves the right one, and introduces a 2. It is therefore NOT a self-map of a single equation, so infinite descent cannot close. The number of available steps is exactly v_2(t).

B.claim: Complete mod-8 analysis of a Beal counterexample, covering every parity configuration. C even: both exponents even is IMPOSSIBLE; x even with y odd forces B = 7 mod 8; both odd forces 8 | A+B. A even (so B, C odd): y,z both odd forces B = C mod 8; y odd with z even forces B = 1 mod 8. By symmetry the same holds with A and B exchanged.
